task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of August 3, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style newspaper explainer answering what remains free in Vellum Step Shoes' revised returns policy and how the choice of refund method changes a customer's options.

facts.text: Vellum Step Shoes revised its online returns policy on July 1, 2026, while retaining free returns at its six stores.
For an ordinary change-of-mind return by mail, the retailer deducts a $6 label charge from a refund to the original payment method.
A customer choosing store credit instead receives the item's full eligible price without that label deduction.
Under the supplied policy, the merchandise portion of a mailed return on a $60 item is $54 back to the original payment method or $60 in store credit.
Those figures exclude separately handled tax adjustments and assume no original delivery charge or discount allocation.
Store credit can be used only with Vellum Step and expires 12 months after issuance under the stated terms.
The policy's 40-day return window and unworn-condition requirement remain unchanged.
The retailer separately provides prepaid labels for items it accepts as faulty or sent in error; the $6 change-of-mind charge does not apply to those returns.
The reporting record contains no finding about how every disputed fault claim is resolved.
The company estimates an average mailing and handling cost of $9.50 for an ordinary posted return, not including the item's resale loss.
That average does not establish the cost or profit on each individual return.
Online sales director Mara Tern says store-credit customers often combine the credit with a later purchase.
Tern said, "A credit keeps the next transaction with us. Cash goes back to whatever the customer needs next."
Customer Iven Sore ordered two sizes because neither was stocked at his nearest branch.
Sore said, "Free in a shop is a different offer when the shop is two buses away."
The nearest branch can accept online returns even if it does not carry that product in its own inventory.
The company's first four-week report shows a lower return rate than the previous four weeks but also a different product and promotion mix.
The company has not isolated the fee's effect on return behavior or published the value of unredeemed new credits.
Vellum Step started as a catalog seller and opened its first physical branch in 2012.
The supplied terms describe this retailer's options rather than legal advice about all retailers' return obligations.

forbidden_additions: Every return costs $6, store credit is cash or credits never expire
A demonstrated causal reduction in returns or identical rights and terms across all retailers
preserve: If quoted: A credit keeps the next transaction with us. Cash goes back to whatever the customer needs next.
If quoted: Free in a shop is a different offer when the shop is two buses away.
The $54 cash-method merchandise refund and $60 retailer credit have different uses.
